<Rep. Richard E. Neal>: H.R. 842 adds multi-cancer early detection (MCED) screening tests as a covered benefit under Medicare, effective January 1, 2029. MCED tests have the potential to concurrently detect multiple cancer types across multiple organ sites. The legislation requires that an MCED test must be cleared under section 510(k), classified under section 513(f)(2), or approved under section 515 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) for Medicare coverage.
Under the Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute (ANS) reported out, Medicare can only pay for one test per year for an individual over 50 years of age and under 65 in 2029 (under 65 of age increases by one year for each succeeding year of coverage, so under 66 in 2030 and so on). Despite this inequitable approach, the bill importantly allows the Secretary to ensure coverage is tailored to patient needs once the clinical evidence is available. Once the tests are recommended by a grade of A or B by the United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF), they will be covered as a preventive service through Medicare's traditional preventive services coverage pathway, and the bill's prescribed age and frequency limitations would not apply but would instead follow the USPSTF recommendations.
The original bill did not limit access to MCED screenings on the basis of age. While Democrats strongly support ensuring access to cancer screenings and unanimously supported the legislation in Committee, it is preferable to not base the determination of access to these MCED screening on an arbitrary age.
Meanwhile, Republicans have actively tried to restrict access to needed, evidence-based care, while decimating the very research infrastructure necessary to bring new scientific innovations to market. Over the last nine months, the Trump Administration has slashed nationwide National Institutes of Health (NIH) funding, terminating hundreds of scientific grants. This rapid disinvestment in scientific research endangers patient care, jobs and the economy and threatens America's world leadership in health care innovation and cures.
CBO recently reported that cuts to the Food and Drug Administration FDA and National Institutes of Health (NIH) will hinder the development of new drugs.\1\ Specifically, cuts resulting in a nine-month increase in FDA review times cuts to preclinical NIH funding will result in 53 fewer newer prescription drugs over the next three decades.
\1\https://www.cbo.gov/system/files/2025-07/61373-Drugs.pdf.
The world's largest public funder of biomedical research, the NIH drives discoveries that lead to life-saving therapies and generates economic growth. NIH funding spurred an estimated $92.89 billion in economic activity in Fiscal Year (FY) 2023 alone. For every $100 million of funding, NIH-supported research generates 76 patents, which create opportunities for an estimated $598 million in further research and development.\2\ In FY 2023 alone, NIH awarded $37.81 billion in research funding across all 50 states and Washington, D.C., supporting 412,041 jobs.\3\
\2\https://www.nih.gov/about-nih/what-we-do/impact-nih-research/ serving-society/direct-econom ic-contributions.
\3\https://www.unitedformedicalresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/ 2024/03/UMR-NIHs-Role-in-Sustaining-the-US-Economy-2024-Update.pdf.
The Trump Administration has terminated hundreds--possibly thousands--of NIH grants for scientific research.\4\ These cuts threaten U.S. leadership in medical research, allowing countries like China to expand their investments in biomedical re-search and surpass the U.S. in developing future treatments and cures.\5\ Leading specialty medical societies have raised the alarm bells:
\4\https://taggs.hhs.gov/Content/Data/HHS_Grants_Terminated.pdf.
\5\Government of China, (2022), 14th Five-Year Plan for Bioeconomy Development, https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/cn/national-legislation/14th-five-year-plan-bioeconomy-development.
The very research that drives medical advancements,
fuels economic growth, and sustains America's
competitive edge will suffer--not because of a lack of
talent or opportunity but because of an arbitrary
policy that undermines the financial sustainability of
research institutions . . . This policy shift would
undermine America's biomedical leadership, erode its
workforce competitiveness, and threaten national
security, ultimately ceding scientific and
technological dominance to global competitors.\6\
\6\https://www.aans.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Physician- Response-to-NIH-Indirect-Cost-Policy-2025-03-05-final.pdf.
Trump Administration policies are threatening clinical trials that patients and families depend on to access to therapies, including cancer prevention and treatment. Researchers may be forced to halt clinical trials abruptly, leaving patients and physicians without other options.\7\ A letter from thousands of patients with rare diseases notes:
\7\https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2025/03/trump-nih-clinical-trials-patient-safey/682217/.
--The removal of key experts at Health and Human
Services Agencies, including NIH, FDA [Food and Drug
Administration], and CDC [Centers for Disease Control
and Prevention]--paired with recent executive orders on
federal funding and communications, compromises our
nation's economic prosperity and threatens the
foundation that enables hope. For children and adults
with rare diseases, even a momentary pause in funding
for these programs and agencies will have devastating,
life-altering consequences.\8\
\8\https://everylifefoundation.quorum.us/campaign/111750/.
Furthermore, cutting funding to U.S research institutions and medical centers will deprive all families of new treatments and medical breakthroughs. Attorneys General from 22 states sued the Trump Administration, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the NIH for unlawfully cutting funds that support cutting-edge medical and public health research at universities and research institutions across the country.\9\
\9\https://www.mass.gov/news/ag-campbell-sues-trump-administration-for-defunding-medical-and-public-health-innovation-research.
The war on ``Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion'' harms product development and scientific knowledge. In March, in an unprecedented move, the NIH abruptly terminated millions of dollars of research awards to scientists related to diversity, equity, and inclusion, in violation of court orders from federal judges, effectively imposing conditions on funding that did not exist at the time the grants were awarded.\10\
\10\https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/03/06/metro/trump-kills-science-funding-dei/.
By terminating programs that ensure robust participation in clinical trials, the Trump Administration is attempting to illegally block companies from complying with clinical trial requirements set by Congress to ensure new therapies have complete information on how they work for all Americans when they come to market. Congress requires drug and device companies to develop diversity plans, which will ultimately enable them to enroll more diverse patient populations in clinical trials and ensure representation of populations, who will use the medical products once approved.\11\ Diverse representation in clinical trials is a scientific necessity. For example, cancer research has shown that the effectiveness of certain treatments can vary based on genetic or ethnic backgrounds, making diverse enrollment critical.\12\
\11\https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/selected-amendments-fdc-act/food-and-drug-omnibus-reform-act-fdora-2022.
\12\https://www.cancer.gov/research/infrastructure/clinical-trials/ nci-supported/nci-match: :text= NCI%2DMATCH%2C%20also%20known%20as,no%20matter%20the%20cancer%20type.
Rolling back programs that ensure clinical trials and other research are representative of the U.S. at large will not only make it harder to recruit a broad array of study participants-- which is a setback for science--but it will also reverse
decades of progress in reducing disparities in health outcomes.
The unprecedented levels of HHS cuts will hinder development, approval, and access to drugs, including biosimilars, potentially increasing risk to patient health and safety. This administration indiscriminately and almost immediately fired thousands of federal workers, including those that oversee medical device safety, food safety, and clinical trials, which will slow innovation and affect the safety and availability of consumer products--including food, drugs, and devices--as well as responses to public health threats, such as influenza, measles, and other infectious disease outbreaks.\13\\14\\15\ Specifically:
\13\https://abcnews.go.com/US/agencies-federal-workers-fired/ story?id=118901289.
\14\https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/18/us/politics/fda-cdc-health-department-trump.html.
\15\https://www.msn.com/en-us/health/other/cdc-invites-back-about- 180-fired-employees-includ ing-some-who-help-fight-outbreaks/ar- AA1Ak2VV?ocid=BingNewsSerp.

world's largest funder of biomedical research in the
nation's development of new drugs. These cuts currently

diseases to study and medicines to develop.\16\
\16\Megan Molteni, et al., Five NIH Institute Directors and Numerous Lab Heads Ousted in Unprecedented Shake-Up, STAT (April 1, 2025), https://www.statnews.com/2025/04/01/nih-rif-1200-layoffs-raise-concerns-health-medicine-biomedical-research/ (last visited April 2, 2025).
• Drastic cuts totaling 19 percent of the Food
and Drug
Administration (FDA) budget will compromise the
agency's
ability to approve new biosimilars and ensure their
safety.
This rollback will erode the agency's core functions,
including
monitoring drug safety, and evaluating and approving
new drugs, devices, and vaccines.\17\ Without qualified
staff to review drug applications and inspect new
manufacturing facilities, patients cannot safely access
these drugs.
\17\Lizzy Lawrence and Sarah Todd, FDA Commissioner Marty Makary Gets Off to a Brusing Start as Agency Is Wracked by Layoffs, STAT (April 1, 2025), https://www.statnews.com/2025/04/01/fda-rif-3500-layoff-notices-under-rfk-jr-hhs-reorganization/ (last visited April 2, 2025).
• Staffing cuts at the CDC will affect the
monitoring of emerging disease and public health
threats.
Republicans have put their extremist views ahead of finding a cure for cancer. President Biden's Cancer Moonshot initiative sought to accelerate development of cures for cancer. It was the largest organized effort ever by the federal government to accelerate cancer research, find cures, and reduce cancer deaths by half within 30 years--and the nearly $2 billion investment received bipartisan support and praise. The program was funded on a bipartisan basis in the 21st Century Cures Act.\18\ Unfortunately, Republicans zeroed out funding for the Cancer Moonshot in March of 2024.\19\
\18\https://www.congress.gov/bill/114th-congress/house-bill/34.
\19\https://www.politico.com/news/2024/04/29/congress-is-killing-bidens-cancer-moonshot-00154718.
